Apple 可以透過多種方式提高 App Store 的利潤率。其中之一是取消人手審查應用程式流程；在代理式編程年代，這個流程不但成本可能高昂，成效亦未必理想。話雖如此，進一步自動化應用程式審查肯定有助節省成本，但用戶大概不會樂見。

Over the past few days, two separate reports have highlighted different ways Apple could boost its profits by growing its services business.

In my view, there's one of those routes that Apple absolutely should take, and one that it absolutely should not — and it looks like Phil Schiller may agree with me…

First, let's recap the two reports.

Home security and monitoring service

Bloomberg reported on Friday that Apple may be planning to launch a brand-new home security and monitoring service, as part of what we expect to be some new home hardware.

Squeezing more revenue from the App Store

A second report from the same outlet on Sunday said that Apple is looking at ways to squeeze more revenue and profit from the App Store.

Apple should not take the latter route

Let's take these in reverse order: I think the second direction would be a huge mistake.

Apple's effective monopoly on iPhone app sales is already under fierce criticism from regulators around the world. In most countries, if you want to sell iPhone apps, you have to go through the official App Store, leaving you with no choice but to accept Apple's terms.

I know many would argue that nobody is forced to buy an iPhone or to develop apps for it, but that's not how genuine free-market capitalism is meant to work: even the US has had antitrust laws since 1890. Once you achieve a certain level of market dominance, your behaviour is constrained to prevent you from abusing that position.

Trying to extract more money from the App Store is the very opposite of "skating to where the puck is going." Reportedly, Phil Schiller shares the same view, and Bloomberg hints that this is one of the reasons for his current retirement.

Innovative services are the right direction

By contrast, launching genuinely innovative new services that customers will want to pay for is the right direction for Apple. I can entirely see the value of Apple offering a home security monitoring service.

I argued back in 2024 that an Apple-branded smart home camera would be one of the smartest moves the company could make. I've said the same about the rumoured Apple smart doorbell. Adding an optional service tie-in to security products makes complete sense, for two reasons.

First, there's the privacy consideration I've raised many times before. HomeKit Secure Video already does a great deal to safeguard the privacy of security camera footage. If I were going to pick a company to carry out AI analysis of security camera footage, I would pick Apple.

Second, Apple is best placed to fully integrate security hardware and services within the HomeKit ecosystem. I believe there are plenty of other areas where Apple could offer a similar advantage.

For me, the key is that Apple needs to treat services with the same attitude it brings to hardware. Make great products, and people will happily — and willingly — part with their cash. Not extract money in ways that leave customers, developers, and regulators feeling annoyed.

If you can be a little patient and not rush to get new Apple products on the first day of sale, Apple's refurbished product store has always been a good choice. Generally speaking, there's usually about a three-month wait between a product's launch and the first batch of refurbished models appearing on Apple's website.

Other companies offer similar options, such as Amazon Renewed and Walmart Restored, but note that they use different standards and warranty policies……

Apple Certified Refurbished Products

Buying from Apple's Certified Refurbished Products store typically gets you about a 15% discount, and the products are completely identical to brand-new units. Specifically, Apple guarantees all of the following:

  • Full inspection and testing by Apple
  • Brand new housing, so there will be no scratches or wear
  • Brand new battery, with battery life identical to a new unit
  • Comes with all original accessories and cables
  • Enjoys Apple's standard one-year warranty, identical to brand-new products
  • Equally eligible for purchasing AppleCare+

Basically, the only difference you'll see is that the product comes in a plain white box rather than original packaging.

Amazon Renewed

Amazon Renewed's pricing can be more attractive, but note that you won't receive the same quality assurance:

  • Inspected and tested by the seller, not by Apple
  • Used housing, so there will be scratches and wear (see details below)
  • Used battery, only guaranteed to have at least 80% of original capacity
  • Accessories may not be original Apple products
  • 90-day Amazon warranty, not Apple's one-year warranty

As for scratches and wear, Amazon offers three tiers:

  • Premium / Excellent: No visible cosmetic damage when viewed from 12 inches away
  • Good: Light scratches only, barely noticeable when holding the device from 12 inches away
  • Acceptable: Scratches easily visible and palpable

Walmart Restored

Walmart Restored's description of what you're getting for your money is far more vague than Amazon's:

  • No commitment on cosmetic condition, only guarantees "like-new performance and reliability"
  • Beyond the above, no details mentioned about battery condition
  • No information provided about accessories
  • Warranty provided by the seller, not Apple's one-year warranty

The Restored Premium tier comes with a one-year seller warranty, while Like New, Good, and Fair tiers only get 90 days. The company doesn't clearly define each tier.

9to5Mac's Take

If you want a product whose appearance and warranty are no different from a brand-new unit, Apple's refurbished store is clearly the first choice.

However, Amazon Renewed's prices can be much cheaper, so if you're willing to accept the trade-offs mentioned above, it can be a pretty good deal. Especially if you follow our advice to save money by upgrading to an iPhone 17 Pro instead of this year's model (you'd only be giving up the (PRODUCT)RED), there are indeed some attractive deals here:

91de1b440b6c.content:
For a long time there have been rumors that Apple is developing a foldable clamshell device, which could be an iPad, a Mac, one of each, or some hybrid of the two.

Recently there were reports that, although this had been a priority project for incoming CEO John Ternus, the project has been shelved—but I don't think that's quite accurate…

Personally, I think the concept of a hybrid Mac and iPad is essentially a thing of the past. Today's Mac can run iPhone and iPad apps, and for many of us iPhone Mirroring is another tool that achieves the same end. We're also seeing increasing convergence between the operating systems, and I believe that trend will continue: we're well past the point where Apple used to argue we were merging a fridge and a toaster.

But I do think that once we have a technology that makes a software keyboard a viable replacement for a hardware keyboard, we'll ultimately end up with an all-screen foldable Mac. It won't happen soon, but it will happen.

Medium-term: the dynamic keyboard

I think it's still a long way off because I believe there will be an interim stage, and that's the dynamic hardware keyboard. I talked about why I think that's the future as long ago as a decade, and although the technology exists in some niche applications, it hasn't yet gone mainstream.

One early attempt was the Sonder Keyboard, which used tiny e-ink displays to remap the labels and functions of the keys.

For someone who spends all day editing in Final Cut Pro, a QWERTY keyboard is of very little use, which is why there's a market for physical keyboards and keyboard covers.

How smart would it be if our MacBook keyboard, or our desktop Magic Keyboard, could automatically re-label itself according to the app in use at the time?

A software keyboard that feels like a hardware one

However, the longer-term goal is a fully software keyboard. Back in 2016 I argued that the case Steve Jobs made for virtual buttons when he introduced the iPhone applies equally to the Mac keyboard.

Of course, there are three problems with a software keyboard:

  • A glass keyboard is uncomfortable to type on
  • We rely on key travel for feedback and comfort
  • Touch typists need to feel the location of a key before pressing it

Apple already has patents addressing each of these. First, using a flexible display rather than conventional glass means the surface can deform when a virtual key is pressed. The second can be addressed by combining that deformation with haptic motors. And for being able to feel a physical key with your fingers, there are two solutions.

Apple's patent uses electrostatic charges to create the sensation of changes in surface texture. In other words, even while the surface remains flat, you can apply charge to the display surface to make it feel like a physical key is there. And in 2023, researchers at Carnegie Mellon came up with an alternative approach.

The question is when, not if

All of these technologies are, of course, still at a very early stage, but you only have to look at the precedent of the Mac trackpad. Trackpads still sound and feel like mechanical devices, but for many years they have been solid-state devices that use haptics to simulate physical clicks—and they do so extremely convincingly.

Software keyboards will eventually reach the same level of maturity. Whether by means of the solutions Apple has so far proposed, or some as-yet-unseen technology, those three problems will be solved.

When that day comes, Steve's argument will apply equally to the Mac. In clamshell mode, the keyboard can take whatever form is appropriate for the work in hand. When all we need is one giant display—whether watching a movie or sketching with an Apple Pencil—we just unfold it and the screen doubles in size.

So I'm fully open to the first-generation model being put on hold for now, but that's absolutely not the same as saying it's been cancelled. This is a technology that will eventually arrive.

Those are my thoughts; what are yours? Please share them in the comments.

週日下午，一架亞馬遜貨運飛機在邁阿密國際機場衝出跑道，撞及多輛汽車，造成至少五人死亡，多人受傷。官員表示。

邁阿密-戴德郡郡長 Daniella Levine Cava 向記者表示：「對邁阿密-戴德郡所有人來說，今天是極其艱難的一天。我們得悉 Prime Air 7598 號航班今早衝出跑道，目前證實有五人罹難，五人受傷。」

她續說：「我的心與所有受影響的家庭，以及今晚正承受哀傷的每一個人同在。我們亦為傷者及其家人祈禱。」

從現場初步拍得的影片可見，一架波音 767-300 客機著陸後側偏跑道，機上冒出火焰及黑色濃煙。

邁阿密-戴德郡警長 Rosie Cordero-Stutz 週日向記者表示：「我們已將多名傷者送往本地醫院，傷勢情況未明」，她補充指，辦公室轄下的兇案調查組將聯同地方及聯邦執法部門負責死亡事故的調查工作。

目前未能確定死者是地面的人抑或機上的人員。Cordero-Stutz 表示現場仍在處理中，警長辦公室已設立熱線，供相信有親友受事件影響的市民查詢。

消防局長 Raied「Ray」Jadallah 確認早前消息，指事故中有多輛汽車被撞及，邁阿密-戴德消防救援隊派出近 200 名人員協助滅火及搜救工作。Jadallah 表示，救援人員協助了數名被困車內的傷者。

局長表示：「我們遇到非常複雜的火警，引擎艙起火，並要展開搜救行動，將被困於飛機內的機長及副機長救出。」

《邁阿密先驅報》取得的緊急無線電通訊錄音中，可以聽到一名消防員向同僚說道：「飛機著火了。飛機著火了。大家打起精神來。」

令情況更為棘手的是，據報消防員在滅火及嘗試救出傷者的過程中，飛機的左引擎仍然在運轉。

美國聯邦航空管理局（FAA）在聲明中表示，21 Air 7598 號航班於當日下午約 2 時降落時衝出跑道，該航班較早時從波多黎各聖胡安的路易斯·穆尼奧斯·馬林國際機場起飛。

美國國家運輸安全委員會（NTSB）表示，已派出小組調查這次墜機事故，並將於週一召開記者會。

亞馬遜發言人 Kelly Nantel 在聲明中表示：「得悉今日於邁阿密國際機場發生的事故導致五人喪生，我們深感悲痛。對於在這場慘痛損失中失去摯愛的家屬，以及所有受影響人士，我們致以最深切的慰問。」

她續說：「肇事飛機由 21 Air 營運，當時正在嘗試降落時發生事故。我們正與地方當局及官員密切合作了解情況，並會全力配合任何調查。」

邁阿密國際機場原先實施地面停飛措施。截至美東時間下午約 6 時 30 分，機場表示四條跑道中已有兩條恢復運作，「但我們仍受到今次事件影響」。

機場在 X 平台發文稱：「原定今日乘搭航班的旅客，請於出發前往機場前，直接向所屬航空公司查詢航班最新狀況。」

在美國，趕喺勞動節週末前出發去最後一趟夏日旅程，入油從來都未試過咁貴。

根據美國汽車協會（AAA）數據，節日前普通汽油平均價為每加侖4.14美元，較去年高出近一美元，亦遠超2012年勞動節週末錄得嘅每加侖3.82美元紀錄。

Nicole Collins原本計劃由費城前往南卡羅來納州探朋友，但佢話因為開車成本太高，一家人成個夏天都留喺屋企附近，無好似平時咁週末出遊。

Collins喺特拉華州Claymont一間油站外接受訪問時表示：「依家油價真係好高，屋企又有BB要照顧，使費更加大。」該油站嘅普通汽油售價為每加侖4.199美元。

今年2月美國同以色列襲擊伊朗之後，油價急升，至今未見回落。經過霍爾木茲海峽嘅原油運輸量大跌，伊朗亦拒絕重新開放該航道。

德州基督教大學能源金融教授Tom Seng話：「一切矛頭都指向伊朗戰事同霍爾木茲海峽問題。」

能源部長Chris Wright未有詳細交代司機幾時可以喺油站見到油價回落，只係承認現時油價高過2025年勞動節水平。

Wright星期日接受ABC節目《This Week》訪問時話：「係嘅，今日油價的確較高，但我哋正竭盡所能壓低油價。」

全國普通汽油平均價仍然遠低於2022年6月創下嘅每加侖5.02美元紀錄。

貨車以及其他貨運系統使用大量柴油，運輸成本上升最終轉嫁到消費者身上，無論係喺超市購物定係使用速遞服務都受影響。

Collins話：「睇起嚟呢個情況根本無結束嘅一日。」

隨住夏季駕駛旺季結束、煉油廠轉為生產較平嘅冬季汽油配方，油價通常會回落。

但Seng指出，今年除咗中東局勢動盪之外，仲有其他因素令未來油價難以預測。美國煉油廠正以98%產能運作，當中好多都位於天氣異常酷熱嘅德州。萬一嗰度出問題或者颶風吹倒部分設施，油價將難以下調。

UNC Charlotte經濟學臨床教授Matthew Metzgar話，問題唔止喺中東。烏克蘭以無人機攻擊俄羅斯煉油廠，令柴油供應緊張；中國煉油廠嘅產量亦正在下降。

Metzgar話：「煉油廠出嚟嘅汽油真係少咗好多。」

能源部長Wright話，特朗普政府正採取措施提高產量，市場預期未來幾個月油價會回落。

佢話：「大家睇下期貨價格，如果你今日大手買入兩個月後即11月交付嘅汽油，每加侖會比今日平大概0.35美元。所以市場認為汽油價格將會顯著回落。」

不過從地緣政治角度睇，一般司機對降低油價幾乎無能為力。

但Metzgar話，使用格價Apps可以幫慳返少少錢，尤其係長途旅行時，高速公路旁嘅油站油價可能會比落一兩個街口嘅油站貴10至15美仙一加侖。

Apple 的 WebKit 團隊現正邀請開發者就 Interop 2027 提交建議，這個跨瀏覽器協作計劃的下一屆活動旨在改善網頁互通性。以下是有關詳情。

少少背景

在過去幾年，Apple 與 Google、Microsoft、Mozilla、Bocoup 以及 Igalia 合作推動 Interop，這是一項每年進行的計劃，目的是令現代網頁技術在不同瀏覽器之間運作得更一致。

該項目於 2022 年展開，奠基於較早前的 Compat 計劃，參與的瀏覽器廠商及機構當年識別出 15 個互通性問題較為嚴重的關鍵領域。Compat 原本只打算進行一次，但成效理想，因此 Interop 自此每年都會續辦。

每年，團隊都會根據網頁開發社群提出的部分建議，揀選一組新的重點領域。瀏覽器廠商其後會致力改善這些領域的實作，並透過同一套 Web Platform Tests 來量度進展。

今年較早前，WebKit 團隊公布了 Interop 2025 的成績，顯示獲選測試在所有瀏覽器中全部通過的比例，由年初的 29% 大幅躍升至年底的 97%。

團隊同時公布了 Interop 2026 選定的 20 個重點領域，涵蓋 CSS 功能以及 Navigation API、View Transitions、WebRTC 和 WebTransport 等技術，當中有部分是根據去年公開徵集期間開發社群提交的建議而訂定。

說到這裏，便要帶出今年的公開徵集。活動已於 9 月 3 日正式開始，截止日期為 9 月 23 日。

Interop 2027 提案現正接受提交

Apple 表示，有關建議必須建基於成熟的網頁標準，並且是可以測試的，因為尚未成熟的技術未適合作為 Interop 重點領域，而計劃需要依賴自動化的 Web Platform Tests 來量度各瀏覽器的進度。公司亦指出，若某項技術缺乏足夠的測試或測試基礎設施，則應改為以 Interop Investigations 的形式提出。

以下是 Apple 所認為一份「出色」的 Interop 2027 提案應具備的元素：

最優秀的提案通常具備以下特點：具體：指出明確的互通性問題。每份提案只針對一項功能（或一組密切相關的功能）。可以 font-size-adjust 為例，而不是籠統地寫「字體排版」。有影響力：清楚描述需要解決的互通性問題，附上你親身遇到的使用個案會更加有幫助。有價值：解釋網頁開發者及／或使用者將如何受惠。相比現有方案，為何這項建議更有價值？有否證據顯示這是普遍需求（例如調查結果）？穩定：連結到定義該技術的穩定版網頁標準。（可在該技術的 MDN 網頁文件中找到，例如這裏。）可測試：查閱並連結相關的 WPT 測試覆蓋範圍。如需更多測試，可如何在今秋補上？閱讀 Interop 提案者指南以了解更多。

公司亦提醒開發者注意，並非每個閱讀今年提案的人都會完全了解去年的提案內容，因此必須「花足夠時間充分闡述」自己的理據。

這包括解釋為何所建議的重點領域十分重要、目前的狀況如何影響網頁開發者與使用者、該技術的應用範圍有多廣，以及相對於其他潛在重點領域，為何這項問題應優先處理。

開發者可透過在 GitHub 開立 issue 提交自己的提案，亦可就現有提案留言，以協助強化其理據。Apple 表示，比起就相同或非常相近的概念提交多份提案，集中貢獻於同一份現有 issue 會更為理想。
